Hadhrat Abu Hurayrah (RA)'s Interpretation of Guarding the Borders during the Time of Rasulullaah ﷺ
Hadhrat Dawood bin Saalih narrates that Hadhrat Abu Salamah once asked him if he knew why Allaah revealed the verse:
Exercise patience, compete in patience, guard the borders...

When Hadhrat Dawood admitted that he did not know, Hadhrat Abu Salamah said, "I heard Hadhrat Abu Hurayrah (RA) say that during the time of Rasulullaah ﷺ there was no war because of which the borders had to be guarded, but waiting for one salaah after another was their form of guarding the borders." [^2]
The Statement of Hadhrat Anas (RA) Concerning the verse "Their sides part from their beds"
Hadhrat Anas (RA) said that it is waiting for the Isha salaah that is referred to in the verse:
Their sides part from their beds...
Emphasis and Importance shown to Performing Salaah in Congregation
The Importance Rasulullaah ﷺ Showed to Salaah in Congregation and His Unwillingness to Allow a Blind Man to Forego it

Hadhrat Amr bin Ummu Maktoom (RA) once said, "O Rasulullaah ﷺ! I am a blind man who lives far (from the Masjid). While I have a guide, he is a person with whom I cannot get along. Are you able to grant me permission to perform salaah at home?" "Can you hear the Adhaan?" Rasulullaah ﷺ asked. When Hadhrat Amr (RA) said that he could, Rasulullaah ﷺ said, "I am then unable to grant you permission." [^4]
